daily_brief: Sunday's news agenda is dominated by escalating US-Russia-Ukraine tensions following President Trump's controversial diesel deal with Moscow. The arrangement, which suspends sanctions on Russian diesel exports, drew sharp condemnation from Ukrainian President Zelensky and EU foreign policy chief Kallas [BBC, RFI, France 24]. Trump responded by suggesting Ukraine needs 'a new president who can make a deal,' while Russia struck Zaporizhzhia with glide bombs, killing at least 20 civilians including four children [BBC Europe]. In the Gulf, a Houthi missile attack on Riyadh's international airport killed 12 people and wounded over 300, marking the deadliest strike on Saudi soil in over a decade and prompting Western leaders to warn of dangerous regional escalation [RFI, Al Jazeera, Globe and Mail]. Pope Leo XIV announced he will undergo surgery after doctors discovered an early-stage lung nodule, with recovery expected within a week [BBC, France 24]. In India, leaders of the youth-led 'Cockroach' movement were released after detention, with protests continuing over alleged electoral misconduct [BBC, ABC Australia]. Pakistan declared emergency rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa province, ending the PTI-led provincial government amid deteriorating security [The Hindu].

top_stories.headline: Trump Calls for Ukraine to Replace Zelensky After Diesel Deal Backlash
bullets: US President Trump announced a deal for Russia to release 300,000+ tonnes of diesel to US markets, with Treasury suspending sanctions on Russian diesel exports until April 7, 2027
Ukrainian President Zelensky condemned the deal as 'a gift to Putin' and 'an investment in a war that must be ended, not prolonged'
Trump responded by saying Zelensky 'better damn well stop' striking Russian refineries and suggested 'it's time for Ukraine to get a new president'
Zelensky later offered to halt refinery strikes if Russia stops attacks on Ukrainian energy infrastructure; EU's Kaja Kallas said Europe 'won't ease pressure on Russia'

top_stories.headline: Houthi Attack on Riyadh Airport Kills 12, Wounds Over 300 in Deadliest Saudi Strike in Decade
bullets: Saturday's missile strike on King Khalid International Airport killed 12 people (including nationals from US, Saudi Arabia, Bangladesh, Jordan, Palestine, Syria, Sudan, Egypt) and wounded over 300
Attack was the third on Riyadh airport this week and deadliest on Saudi soil in more than a decade; no warning was issued by Saudi threat warning system
UN Secretary General Guterres called attacks 'a violation of international law'; EU's von der Leyen called it a 'dangerous escalation'
Saudi-led coalition vowed to 'firmly' retaliate; Houthis have not claimed responsibility but warned airlines against using Saudi airports

top_stories.headline: Russian Glide Bomb Attack on Zaporizhzhia Kills at Least 20, Including Four Children
bullets: Russia struck Ukrainian city of Zaporizhzhia with five glide bombs Saturday morning, hitting residential buildings
At least 20 killed including four children; 32+ injured with more believed trapped under rubble
Zelensky said attacks were Russia 'expressing thanks' for Trump's diesel deal and evidence Russia takes 'any easing of pressure to mean they can keep fighting'
Acting Mayor said apartment block collapsed from ground floor up; over 80 rescue workers searching for survivors

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Detailed reporting on casualties and rescue operations; included Zelensky's political framing

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Noted death toll rising to 23 by Sunday; covered in context of Zelensky's conditional offer to halt strikes

top_stories.headline: Pope Leo XIV to Undergo Surgery After Early-Stage Lung Nodule Detected
bullets: Pope Leo XIV, 71, announced during Sunday Angelus prayers that doctors found 'an early, well-localised nodule' on his lung during routine medical checks
Surgery scheduled for early next week at Rome's Gemelli Hospital; expected recovery time approximately one week
Leo, born Robert Francis Prevost, became the first American pope in May 2025 following the death of Pope Francis
Vatican Press Office confirmed the mass was 'well-contained' and caught 'at an early stage'

top_stories.headline: India Releases 'Cockroach Party' Leaders as Youth Protests Continue Over Electoral Misconduct Allegations
bullets: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke and two other leaders released Sunday after being detained upon arrival in Delhi Saturday; released on condition they 'not engage in breach of peace for one year'
Reports indicate 7,000 protesters were detained and released Saturday; hundreds more detained Sunday as thousands of security personnel deployed
Movement demands resignation of Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar over allegations of manipulating voter rolls, which Election Commission denies
Opposition leader Rahul Gandhi also detained; CJP vowed to continue protests with Dipke stating 'Modi, as PM, is an embarrassment to India'
